intent: Quiet documentary dread that turns into tenderness: the audience should feel the weight of a decision nobody thanked him for.
pacing_profile: slow-burn: hushed tense open, urgent peak at the launch count (v03), suspended silence after the decision (v06), then slower and warmer to a reverent close
pause_policy: Pauses carry the story: a held breath after the false-alarm report, longer silences once the story turns personal (v08-v10), and the longest hold at the very end. Never pause mid-phrase except at marked ellipses.

lines.text: Just after midnight, on September 26th, 1983… a computer told one man that America had launched a nuclear missile.
lines.direction: Low and close, as if telling a secret. Let the date land, breathe, then a level, almost flat 'nuclear missile'.

lines.text: Weeks earlier, Soviet jets had shot down a passenger plane. Two hundred and sixty-nine people died. The Cold War was at its most paranoid.
lines.direction: Matter-of-fact context; a small weight on 'two hundred and sixty-nine'. No drama on 'paranoid'.

lines.text: The screen lit up: LAUNCH. Then a second missile. A third. A fourth. A fifth.
lines.direction: The only fast line. Each count a notch tighter, like an alarm repeating.

lines.text: His job was to pass it up the chain… to leaders who might have only minutes to decide whether to strike back.
lines.direction: Explain the stakes plainly; the pause after 'chain' lets the viewer picture the ladder.

lines.text: But Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov had a funny feeling in his gut. "When people start a war," he said, "they don't start it with only five missiles."
lines.direction: Introduce him with respect. The quote is calm logic, not heroics.

lines.text: So he reported a false alarm. And then… he waited. Twenty-three minutes. Nothing came.
lines.direction: Slow down. The ellipsis is a held breath; 'Twenty-three minutes' stretched; 'Nothing came' almost whispered, then silence.

lines.text: It was sunlight. Reflecting off high clouds, at a rare angle, fooling a satellite.
lines.direction: The reveal: a beat after 'sunlight', then an almost wondering tone.

lines.text: There was no medal. He was reprimanded for incomplete paperwork. And the story stayed secret for fifteen years.
lines.direction: Dry irony on 'paperwork', no sarcasm. Let 'fifteen years' sit.

lines.text: For ten years, his own wife knew nothing. When she asked what he'd done, he said: "Nothing. I did nothing."
lines.direction: Warm and quiet, like remembering someone. A gentle half-smile on 'I did nothing'.

lines.text: He died in 2017, so quietly the world only found out months later. One obituary said he was survived by two children, two grandchildren… and the entire human race.
lines.direction: The emotional peak. Unhurried. A real held beat before 'and the entire human race', delivered softly with a lift of wonder, not volume.
